claims.text: CrCoNi has superior work hardening and ductility compared with equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
Equiatomic ternaries related to CrCoNi generally have superior work hardening and ductility compared with CrMnFeCoNi.
Removing Mn minimizes magnetic frustration in CrCoNi.
CrCoNi has a lower-energy HCP phase than its FCC phase.
Mechanical deformation induces an FCC-to-HCP transformation in CrCoNi.
The HCP phase forms along dislocation structures and internal boundaries.
The deformation-induced transformation interacts with dislocation motion to enhance strain hardening and delay failure.
Magnetically frustrated Mn eliminates the FCC-HCP energetic distinction and suppresses the HCP transformation in CrMnFeCoNi.
CrMnFeCoNi lacks transformation-induced strengthening and remains predominantly FCC during the specified deformation.
Thermomechanically processed CrCoNi and CrMnFeCoNi can both be prepared as single-phase FCC solid solutions.
The compared CrCoNi and CrMnFeCoNi specimens have similar grain sizes.
Dislocation slip is the dominant deformation mechanism under quasi-static room-temperature loading for the stated alloys.
Other equiatomic ternary derivatives of CrMnFeCoNi should exhibit the same measurable FCC-to-HCP transformation as CrCoNi.
CrCoNi should have a higher strain-hardening rate than CrMnFeCoNi under identical loading.
CrCoNi should have greater tensile ductility than CrMnFeCoNi under identical loading.
The magnitude of the mechanical effect and the threshold transformation strain may depend on additional processing variables.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and prediction generalize the transformation mechanism to related ternaries, whereas the mechanism is specifically developed for Mn-free CrCoNi. The cited evidence further states that the transformation occurs only in CrCoNi and distinguishes it from the other equiatomic ternary derivatives.
